subject: Automotive & EVs
title: The Daytona 500
description: A quick win: understand The Daytona 500.

hook.text: NASCAR's biggest race is held on a 2.5-mile superspeedway where cars hit 200 mph in packs.

buildup.text: Daytona's steep 31-degree banking lets cars run flat out without lifting, separated by inches.

discovery.text: Drafting—tucking behind another car to cut air resistance—is so powerful it defines every strategy.

twist.text: The pack racing creates spectacular crashes when one car's wobble triggers a chain reaction at 200 mph.

climax.text: Dale Earnhardt's fatal crash in the 2001 Daytona 500 transformed NASCAR's approach to driver safety.

punchline.text: The Great American Race is both the most watched and most feared.

quiz.question: What racing technique defines strategy at Daytona?
